title: Lions Club plants a community garden at Rowlett's oldest church
excerpt: Rowlett Lions are building raised garden beds at First Christian Church, home of the Hope in Hand Food Pantry.
coverAlt: Three Rowlett Lions Club volunteers, two in yellow Lions vests, shoveling soil into new green raised garden beds
body:
Some of the best good news starts with a shovel.

The Rowlett Lions Club has a new project: a community garden at First Christian Church, home of the Hope in Hand Food Pantry. Working alongside LaKisha Kabinga, Lions volunteers have been filling a row of new raised garden beds with soil, getting them ready to grow.

"We are so excited," said Lions Club member Amparo Ocampo.

It's a fitting place for it. The Hope in Hand Food Pantry at First Christian Church serves families in Rowlett, Garland, Sachse and Rockwall, and a garden right next door is a natural partner for a pantry that feeds its neighbors.

It's also a fitting church for it. First Christian is Rowlett's oldest congregation, founded in 1893, when Rowlett was a farming town of fewer than 1,000 people growing cotton, corn and onions. More than 130 years later, the church is helping Rowlett grow food again.

If you've been to the Rowlett Chamber of Commerce, you've already been inside a piece of that history. First Christian's 1923 church building, which served the congregation for more than 70 years, now houses the Chamber's offices, a Rowlett treasure that's still serving the community today.

And it's one more reason to be thankful for the Rowlett Lions, the same club that gave nearly $46,000 back to the community this year.

Want to help, or know a family the pantry could serve? Contact First Christian Church at 7301 Miller Road.
